title: The Manifesto for Teaching and Learning in a Time of Generative AI: A Critical Collective Stance to Better Navigate the Future
extended_summary:
This paper is a manifesto that critically examines the rapid integration of generative AI (GenAI), chatbots, and algorithms into education, with a particular focus on teaching and learning in higher education. Rather than evaluating a specific intervention, the authors argue for a balanced, evidence-based, and ethically grounded stance toward GenAI, emphasizing that these systems are not neutral and may reshape pedagogy, assessment, agency, equity, and human relationships in education.

The paper uses collective writing and a modified Delphi process to synthesize the perspectives of a large international group of higher-education educators and researchers specializing in GenAI. The resulting themes outline both perceived benefits and risks: on the positive side, GenAI may save time, support personalized learning, assist lesson planning and formative feedback, improve accessibility, and foster creativity and innovation; on the negative side, it may deepen digital divides, amplify bias, undermine academic integrity, spread misinformation, reduce human connection, and weaken critical thinking and learner agency.

The context is explicitly higher education and broader educational policy/practice, not K-12 literacy instruction. The authors conclude that GenAI should be integrated cautiously, with human oversight, institutional support, transparent policies, and ongoing research. They argue that GenAI should augment rather than replace human teaching, and that educators should preserve care, equity, creativity, and critical reflection while adapting curricula, assessment, and professional practice to the realities of GenAI.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI / large language model chatbot systems that can generate text and other content, support conversation, and assist with tasks such as drafting, feedback, and personalization.
identified_tools.use_case: This manifesto discusses generative AI broadly, including chatbots and LLMs such as ChatGPT, as an educational technology that may support lesson planning, formative feedback, assessment, tutoring, and other teaching/learning functions. It does not evaluate a specific product or report empirical effects.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a manifesto/editorial and qualitative collective-writing piece, not an empirical evaluation of a specific AI tool. It offers critical discussion and thematic claims rather than measured outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper argues GenAI may have broad educational influence, but it provides no quantitative effect estimates or outcome data. Its influence is conceptual and field-shaping rather than evidence of measured impact.
